az_cwm_laude_wall.blurb: A compact trad wall at the western end of the sunny north rim of Volunteer Canyon, in the basalt country northern Arizona is known for. Nine routes climb streaked, lichen-covered columns, corners and aretes about 50 to 80 feet tall, and the lines sit close together. The grade range is wide, from a few moderate leads in the 5.6 to 5.9 range through a cluster of 5.10s, with a couple of 5.12 and 5.13 routes at the top end. It is overshadowed by the taller walls beside it, but the climbing is the draw.

az_assorted_goods_boulder.blurb: One of the more photogenic blocks in the Beardsley bouldering zone on the northern edge of Phoenix, sitting right beside the main trail so it is easy to spot. It holds nine short problems, all in the easy range: one at the very bottom of the scale, a handful around V0 and a handful around V1. That makes it a friendly warm-up stop or a place for newer boulderers. The surrounding granite is coarse and weathered desert rock that is tough on skin, boulders in the area reach around 15 feet, and a pad is worth bringing. Grades in this zone run old-school, so easy numbers can feel stiffer than expected.

az_schlotski_roof.blurb: A small, quiet bouldering spot tucked into Howard Draw, part of the Priest Draw system near Flagstaff at roughly 7,000 feet. The centerpiece is a modest roof with moderate lines, ringed by other blocks that offer easy jug traverses. Nine problems in all, running from around V1 up to a handful in the V4 to V7 range, so there is something for a mixed group though the middle grades dominate. The setting feels secluded and has decent shade, which helps on warm days. Plan on a walk of roughly a quarter of an hour or more along the draw trail past the better-known roof and traverse before the path forks right.

az_sahuaro_corners.blurb: A small crag in La Milagrosa Canyon, at the foot of the Santa Catalina Mountains outside Tucson, named for a lone saguaro on the ledge where the routes begin. Seven sport lines and two trad routes fill the wall, graded from 5.10 through the 5.11s with one 5.12, so it suits climbers already comfortable at the harder end of the moderate range rather than beginners. It faces more sun than the neighboring Main Wall, which makes it a warm choice, and the holds are juggier than next door. Reach it by dropping into the creek bed and following the trail past the Main Wall; getting onto the platform takes a couple of technical moves.

az_boat_launch_boulders_the.blurb: A small cluster of low boulders at Blue Ridge Reservoir, a pine-ringed lake in the hills of northern Arizona, roughly 45 miles southwest of Winslow. The blocks sit between the boat ramp and the dam, a short stroll north from the launch. Nine problems, almost all very easy: one at the bottom of the scale, then a spread of V0 and V1 with a single V2. That suits beginners, kids and anyone wanting a casual session before a swim. Landings can change as the water rises and falls, so check the ground before you commit. The reservoir is mostly thought of as a summertime destination.

az_peavine_dome.blurb: A sunny, south-facing granite dome among the Granite Dells crags near Prescott, at about 5,200 feet. It is a sport venue with nine routes, mostly beginner and intermediate: a few at the easy end around 5.6 and 5.7, a couple in the 5.8s and one 5.9, and two at the 5.10 level. One line can also be top-roped. A 60 m rope and around ten draws cover it. Access is the appeal and the hurdle: you walk or bike north along the flat rail-trail from the trailhead, then branch off just past a bridge to reach the base.
az_peavine_dome.parking_note: Leave the car at the Peavine Trailhead in Prescott, the main parking spot for the crags along the Peavine Trail.

az_mr_meanor_wall.blurb: A friendly wall in the Prison Camp area on Mount Lemmon's Catalina Highway, at about 4,700 feet above Tucson. Nine routes, mostly trad with one sport line and one top-rope, run from 5.4 up to 5.10, with the bulk in the easy-to-moderate range, so it works well for newer leaders and for groups building experience. The rock is solid with decent friction. The face catches early shade and is otherwise sunny. Parties commonly shift ropes between the anchors to top-rope the traditional lines. Getting there means a walk along the often-dry riverbed past the other crags, with the wall on your left.

az_choo_choo_rock.blurb: A small crag on the lower stretch of the Catalina Highway on Mount Lemmon, in Sonoran Desert terrain with saguaros and warm temperatures, which makes it a winter-leaning stop. Nine routes split between trad and sport, graded from 5.8 through the 5.9s and 5.10s, so it fits climbers who lead moderately. Rock quality on this part of the mountain is more variable than higher up, so look closely at what you are pulling on. Expect a scrambly approach that involves crossing a wash and following cairns up to the base.

_conflicts.az_boat_launch_boulders_the: Stored rock is sandstone, but the Blue Ridge Reservoir page (https://www.mountainproject.com/v/107729153) describes the boulders rimming the lake as limestone; the area page itself (https://www.mountainproject.com/area/107666776/the-boat-launch-boulders) names no rock.
